claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy has a conventional coarse-grained structure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits higher friction and wear at extreme temperatures.
Sliding-induced dynamic grain refinement can cause interfacial amorphization in CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will form an ultrafine-grained or amorphous surface layer.
The resulting surface layer will be self-lubricating.
The refined or amorphous surface layer will alter contact mechanics.
The nanostructured amorphous layer will reduce interfacial shear strength.
Reduced interfacial shear strength and self-lubrication will lower friction.
Reduced interfacial shear strength and self-lubrication will lower wear.
The intervention will produce a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will reduce wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The friction and wear improvements will persist from room temperature to 800 °C.
The friction and wear improvements will persist under varied loads.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically shows increased friction and wear at both low- and high-temperature extremes.
The intervention is effective from room temperature to 800 °C under the tested loads and controlled environments.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on amorphization kinetics and micromechanical interactions under varying test conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mechanism describe a layer generated in situ by sliding, whereas the experiment compares specimens with and without unspecified pre-induced conditions favoring refinement. It is unclear whether the tested intervention is pretreatment or sliding-induced transformation.
